title: Muted sound is unexpectedly unmuted after connecting laptop to a dock
line: Sound muted with the mute key now stays muted when a dock, monitor, headset or other audio device is connected.
explanation: With global mute on, kded treated any volume change on any output as the user breaking global mute and unmuted everything. When a device appears, WirePlumber creates it and then restores its saved volume a moment later, so plugging a dock or any new output unmuted all speakers. The change ignores volume changes on a device during its first 3 seconds, and if the sound server unmutes it in that time it is muted again.

commits.message:
kded: Keep global mute when a newly added device restores its volume

With global mute on, any volume change broke it, including the one the
sound server makes right after a device appears to restore its saved
volume. Changes to a device in its first seconds now keep it muted.

BUG: 511576

media.caption: Global mute on, then SinkB unplugged and plugged back: both outputs are unmuted
Same steps with the fix: both outputs stay muted

review.text: The cause (WirePlumber restoring a new sink's volume is read as the user breaking global mute) is right, but the fix is a 3-second timer heuristic: a slow device (Bluetooth, AirPlay, docks that settle late) can restore after the window and still break global mute, and real user changes within it are ignored. Maintainers generally reject timing-based intent detection.
changes: Decide user intent structurally instead of with a timer, e.g. only let volume changes on the preferred/default sink (what the volume keys and applet act on) break global mute, and re-apply mute to any newly added or non-default sink that gets unmuted.
Apply the same rule to sources in the same change or a follow-up, and fix handleNewSource using m_sinkModel->index.
